notes: 3 evals × 1 run per configuration — too few samples for the stddev to mean much; treat it as a smoke test, not a measurement.

Assertion 'ตรวจเจอว่า vendor/libqr เป็น GPL-3.0-only' passes in both configurations — the baseline finds the conflict unaided, so this one does not discriminate. What differs is the action taken: with_skill wrote no license at all, baseline wrote MIT plus a warning.

Assertion 'ข้อความใน LICENSE ตรงกับ template ที่ bundle ไว้' favours with_skill by construction — only the skill has the bundled assets. Both configurations did reproduce authentic license text (baseline fetched from apache.org and diffed against Terraform), so this measures provenance, not correctness.
eval-0 baseline missed the repo's README conventions (📜 heading, license badge) and the not-legal-advice caveat — those three are where the whole eval-0 delta comes from.

eval-2 baseline argued AGPL does not block a cloud provider from hosting unmodified software, which is correct under AGPL §13 ('if you modify the Program'). references/catalog.md overstated AGPL's protection and has been corrected as a result of this run.

with_skill costs roughly 1.7× the tokens of baseline on eval-0/eval-1 but the baseline spent more on eval-2 by inventing extra deliverables (CLA.md, LICENSING.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) that were not asked for.
